newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bank Queensland sees profit slump.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bank Queensland sees profit slump.

text.p: Bank of Queensland Ltd said on Friday it expected its half year profit ending on February 28 was likely to be about 25 percent below the year-ago result.
The bank also said it planned a special dividend of 65 cents a share.
The bank said its profit for the second half of the financial year was expected to be above that for the first half, but still below the previous corresponding period.
Bank of Queensland reported a net profit for the first half of 1995/96 of A$10.2 1 million and an operating profit of A$17.81 million.
Directors said the business was growing strongly compared with the year-ago period and they expected to maintain the current dividend rate of 28 cents per share, fully franked.
The bank said it had decided to pay the special fully franked dividend as it was strongly capitalised, with a capital adequacy ratio of 13.0 percent at November 30, 1996.
This was substantially above the bank's business needs, it said.
The special dividend is payable on July 1 to shareholders registered by June 13.
Bank of Queensland is due to release its half-yearly results on April 4.
